find_prospects.description: Search LinkedIn for people matching a query and write everyone found into the project's people/companies graph. A read: it changes nothing on LinkedIn, needs no approval, and costs no touch budget. Run this before proposing a campaign — the rows it leaves are what the CRM shows and what enrolment reads from.

connection_id.description: the connected LinkedIn account to search from

query.description: free text — the single most effective filter

location.description: city or region; folded into the keywords, not a structured filter

start.description: offset, for the next page of the same search

propose_campaign.description: Draft an outreach campaign — the sequence, the per-prospect copy — and put ONE approval in front of the founder. Sends nothing.

advance_sequences.description: The five-minute outreach tick. Harness work, not agent work: the copy was approved days ago, so no model is invoked. Spawned by the sequencer's own schedule — do not create these by hand.

gtm_autonomous.description: One turn of the autonomous GTM loop: FullEnrich discovery from the project's stored audience, then — if it found people the project has not seen — a normal propose_campaign approval. Harness work, not agent work; spawned by the audience's own schedule when the founder enables it. Discovers and proposes only; every send still waits for the founder's approval envelope. Do not create these by hand.

outreach_touch.description: One dispatched step of one prospect's sequence. The anchor an auto-approval, a timeline entry and an audit row hang off. Created by the sequencer, or by a founder taking the touch off their next-move list before the cadence gets to it.
outreach_touch._comment: A ROW, NOT A RUN, which is why there is no `harness` block and no `output_schema` here. The copy was written and approved before the founder said yes, so nothing is drafted at dispatch time and no model is invoked — this task exists so that every message the campaign produced stays individually inspectable afterwards. What it therefore owes is an INPUT contract, and `required` states it: the next-move engine proposes exactly this shape (see `gtmMove` in moves.ts), and a field missing from it is a touch nobody could reconstruct later. moves.test.ts holds the declaration and the proposal to each other.

propose_reply.description: After a prospect replies, draft ONE follow-up DM for human approval. Outside the campaign envelope — the sequence has already stopped, so each send is a new decision until they are booked, won or lost. Nothing goes out until a human approves the exact words.

workflows.name: next_touch
workflows.description: Whether to send the next outbound touch, which stage to move to, and how long to wait. ALWAYS call this before drafting a follow-up; it stops on reply, on booking, and on opt-out.
